basis: Congenital muscle dystrophy with contractures and joint laxity; hypoventilation in 1/3 reflects respiratory muscle weakness rather than intrinsic lung damage.
Hereditary spastic paraplegia with pyramidal dysfunction; spasticity and lower-limb hyperreflexia in 4/4.
Cataract, hypothyroidism and fixed contractures each reported in 1/1; low B-cell count also reported, omitted under four-axis cap. Evidence is a single patient.
Glycosylation defect with cardiomyopathy (80-99%) and ichthyosis (3/4); seizures/developmental delay 30-79%; hepatic enzyme elevations omitted at cap.
Uterine cervix is a reproductive organ outside the 13 axes; no other organ involvement defines this umbrella.
Acute myeloid malignancy of blood and marrow; possible disseminated intravascular coagulation remains within the haematologic axis.
Mitochondrial energy-metabolism disorder; leukoencephalopathy 6/6 and developmental regression with spastic tetraplegia 7/7.
Immune-mediated hypersensitivity pneumonitis directly inflames pulmonary alveoli after occupational antigen exposure.
B-cell lymphoma is a haematologic malignancy and qualifies for the lymphoma mechanism axis; breast itself has no axis.
Autoimmune inflammatory disease of muscle and skin; anti-Mi2 disease has substantially less ILD than other dermatomyositis subtypes, generally below 30%.
Umbrella immunodeficiency encompassing hyper-IgM and hyper-IgE syndromes; direct skin or pulmonary damage is not established in most across the group.
Friedreich phenotype includes cardiomyopathy (~60-70%) and skeletal deformities (>30%); both supported by listed phenotypes, but FRDA2-specific frequencies uncertain.
Combined immunodeficiency and bronchiectasis define the syndrome; cancer predisposition is a later risk, not established organ damage.
Inherited diffuse thickening of palm and sole epidermis; hearing loss and neuropathy occur in selected subtypes rather than most of the umbrella.
Adrenal cortisol excess directly causes myopathy/bone loss (>50%), hypertension (~80%) and skin atrophy/bruising (~50-80%); later vascular events excluded.
Benign NK-cell lymphoproliferative disease infiltrating gastrointestinal mucosa; it is not lymphoma and has no established infectious or autoimmune mechanism.
Inflammation directly affects the uvea, usually through immune-mediated or infectious mechanisms; associated systemic diseases are separate conditions.
Clonal mast-cell disease with another haematologic neoplasm; listed hepatic, skeletal, skin and gastrointestinal manifestations are occasional (5-29%).
Endocardial fibroelastosis and abdominal aortic coarctation directly affect the heart and aorta; associated valve dysfunction shares this axis.
Neurodevelopmental disorder causing persistent impairment of information processing and academic learning.
Structural hair-shaft abnormalities, sparse brittle hair and xeroderma define this skin and hair disorder.
Congenital bilateral ptosis and recurrent laryngeal nerve paralysis define the syndrome; vocal cord dysfunction and frequent laryngomalacia affect the airway.
Malignancy affecting colon or rectum; other listed cancers are separate diseases, and lymphoma is a minority subtype of this umbrella.
Inherited organic acidemia supported by lactic acidosis; respiratory distress alone does not establish direct pulmonary damage.
Malignant tumour of peripheral nerve sheath origin; mediastinal location alone does not establish lung involvement.
